translations.literal: As the world by two poles is sustained, so the law of God, by love of God and of neighbour; by these two foundations it is bound; the machine of the world falls if one of the poles is disturbed; the divine law perishes if one of these.
translations.note: 'vincitur' is read as the passive of vincio, 'is bound', not of vinco, 'is conquered'. The last clause stops at 'si una ex his' ('if one of these'), so 'fails' has been supplied from the parallel clause before it. Burton's main text states the twofold commandment, but this note adds a simile of its own and does not render it.
translations.text: As the world is upheld by two poles, so the law of God is upheld by love of God and of our neighbour; it is bound by these two foundations. The fabric of the world collapses if one of the poles is disturbed; the divine law perishes if one of these fails.
